s1.syndrome_frame: Progressive asthenia, anorexia, and weight loss with hypercalcemia and renal failure
salient_findings: Progressive asthenia, anorexia, and 7-kg weight loss
Osteolytic lesions in the skull bones
key_facts: 53-year-old woman with type 2 diabetes, hypertension, and bipolar disorder
Acute functional renal failure (creatinine clearance 30 mL/min)
No monoclonal peak on serum or urine immunoelectrophoresis
Received IV saline and one dose of zoledronate with initial normalization of calcium and renal function
CT scan showed osteolytic lesions in the skull bones and hypodense micronodules in the liver and spleen
Brain MRI showed T2-hyperintense, T1-isointense, gadolinium-enhancing lesions in the skull
DEXA scan revealed osteopenia (lumbar spine T-score –2.4)
Mammography, esophagogastroduodenoscopy, and colonoscopy were normal
Bone marrow biopsy and labial salivary gland histology were unremarkable
Percutaneous fine-needle aspiration of the liver showed noncaseating granulomatous hepatitis without malignancy

raw.syndrome_frame: Progressive asthenia, anorexia, and weight loss with hypercalcemia and renal failure

Osteolytic lesions in the skull bones

CT scan showed osteolytic lesions in the skull bones and hypodense micronodules in the liver and spleen
Brain MRI showed T2-hyperintense, T1-isointense, gadolinium-enhancing lesions in the skull
DEXA scan revealed osteopenia (lumbar spine T-score –2.4)

raw.rationale: The presence of noncaseating granulomatous hepatitis, hypercalcemia with low PTH, and osteopenia, along with the absence of malignancy on extensive imaging and biopsies, supports the diagnosis of sarcoidosis, which is known to cause these manifestations.

rejected.label: Multiple Myeloma
rejected.why: Normal serum free light-chain ratio and no monoclonal peak on serum or urine immunoelectrophoresis make this diagnosis unlikely

rejected.label: Lymphoma
rejected.why: No evidence of malignancy on imaging, biopsies, or laboratory tests

rejected.label: Malignancy-associated hypercalcemia
rejected.why: No primary malignancy identified despite thorough evaluation

rejected.label: Parathyroid hormone-related protein-producing tumor
rejected.why: Low PTH levels and lack of evidence for a PTHrP-producing tumor
